comments: Combined experiment: bottleneck_kernel_size=3 (the one architecture change with a real from-scratch win, 0.3156 vs baseline's 0.3070 -- never before combined with finetune) + finetune init (via kurals/expand_kernel3.py, which randomly reinitializes only bott_c/d1/d2's dw conv weight -- the sole kernel-size-dependent keys -- and transfers everything else from the native checkpoint unchanged; verified strict-loadable) + three regularizers: weight_decay=1e-3 (a middle value -- 1e-4 measurably did nothing against finetune, 1e-2 measurably hurt it, see kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_finetune_wd.json), dropout_rate=0.1 (new bott_dropout, whole-channel Dropout2d on the bottleneck output, identity at eval so it never reaches the exported NPU graph), label_smoothing=0.1 (via NBSLoss's underlying CrossEntropyLoss, train-time only -- Tester.predict()'s own define_loss call is unaffected, so val/test loss stays computed against true hard labels). Every individual regularizer tried alone against plain finetune so far (weight_decay, data augmentation, longer schedule, shallower architecture) has underperformed 0.3684 -- this tests the specific combination of kernel3 (the one architecture change with real signal) with lighter-touch versions of the regularizers, not a repeat of any single prior negative result.
